correctness.rationale: Re-read complete 24-row CERTIFICATE.json at frozen Git blob SHA 4e9d927279ec0d4bf4117daee2124dea5be530cc. Independently multiplied all 24 primitive integer factor arrays and recomputed their factor-degree profiles; independent SymPy factorizations/discriminants agree. A separate from-scratch finite-field modular polynomial verifier recomputed all 56 specified squarefree Frobenius prime/cycle witnesses for all 28 distinct nonlinear factors: 28 irreducibility types, 4 three-cycles, 8 primitivity and 16 transposition witnesses. Modular irreducibility proves Q irreducibility via Gauss lemma. Prime-degree transitive S7 subgroups are primitive and the 5,2 cycle produces a transposition; transitive sextics with a 5-cycle are primitive and their 3,2,1 cycle produces a transposition, hence symmetric. A quartic 4-cycle and 3-cycle force S4; cubic discriminants -23/-31 force S3. In reducible products, their inequivalent quadratic discriminant subfields (-23 versus -31 or 257) exclude every nontrivial common Galois quotient of S3,S3/S4, so the full products follow. The certificates cover the finite 24-element parameter domain exhaustively; irreducibility and Galois implications are mathematical theorems, not inferred from sample frequencies.

value.rationale: The complete small-height septic boundary lies directly below the recent large-degree maximality theorem and includes unexpected reducible factor profiles. Identifying the precise Galois groups and proving independent splitting fields is a motivated arithmetic refinement over a simple factorization list; it is a finite but natural full 24-case classification.

final_claim: Across the 24 polynomials x^7+a x^k+b, 1<=k<=6, a in {+2,-2}, b in {+1,-1}, the exact splitting-field Galois groups are eight S7, eight S6, four S3 x S3 and four S3 x S4; in two-nonlinear-factor cases the splitting fields are linearly disjoint over Q.
limitations: Only degree exactly seven and a=±2, b=±1; no assertion for all degree-seven trinomials or higher coefficients.
A general height-two factorization database or older small-degree group catalogue could have equivalent entries even without matching family wording.
